How the day works

Your car was loaded this morning in delivery order. Each label carries a stop number and a shelf code: R is the curb side, L the street side, sections 1–8 run from the cab to the rear door, then TOP / MID / BOT. Letters ride in the bin up front. Heavy pieces sit on the floor by the rear door. The preload isn't perfect, so now and then a piece is in the wrong bay.

W A S DDrive (arrows work too). Hold S to brake, then reverse. SpaceSet or release the parking brake. Stop first. EOpen the cargo hold (parked only). Click pieces to pick them up. Click a houseWalk to that door with what you're carrying. Click several to deliver a loop. FWalk to the targeted stop, or call yourself back to the truck. Out on foot a long way from it, F calls the truck to you instead. N / BNext or previous stop on the handheld. L opens the full stop list. L at speedDrift. Hold it near top speed (or on turbo) and steer: the back end slides out and you steer it through; let go to straighten. Off the clock, a good slide tops up the turbo. CSwitch between chase, high and overhead cameras. Mouse wheel or +/- zooms. RGo fishing. On foot, walk up to the river, the bay, a creek or a pond and a button appears. The tackle box is free. Esc packs up. H on a launch matHang glide. There are launches at the Crest Park overlook, Sunset Point and Quarry Hill; walk onto the mat. A D lean, W speeds up, S slows and flares. Land on the orange X, or anywhere open. Z in the woodsOn foot among the trees a button offers the lawn chair. Unfold it, sit back and listen to the birds. Z or any move gets you up. 1 2 3 4 on footWave, nod, shake your fist, or throw a punch (it barely lands). People answer: a wave back, a nod, a few step away and a few square up. Shake a fist at the wrong person and you may be called out to a duel. The buttons are on the right of the screen. GAnswer a prompt when one pops up on screen, like chasing a porch pirate on foot. Ignore it and it goes away by itself. MRoute map. H horn (people on the sidewalk look up). Esc menu.

Red-striped labels have a deadline (most are 10:30). Blue S means a signature is required. Businesses keep hours; the diner and bakery close early, the theater opens late. Afternoon pickups show up on the board, and Dale on the radio may add more or bump a stop up. Avenues stop at every crossing, and so does Main St downtown. Country roads are faster but watch for cows. Dogs, odd neighbors and unhappy customers turn up at the door: pick how you handle them.

Every day brings its own weather. Rain and snow mean longer stops and slides, and fog shrinks what you can see. Orange barricades close a few streets, so plan detours (they show on the map). Some customers leave delivery notes on the handheld; read them before you walk up. After three, a school bus runs near the school, and red lights mean you stop. A freight line runs along Quarry Rd: when the gates come down, wait. Downtown crosswalks fill up with school classes, walking clubs and the occasional family of ducks, and cyclists share the road, so give them room. Parked cars narrow the side streets, so ease toward the center line to get around them, like you would in a real truck. Mailboxes, trash cans, signs, fences and yard things break if you hit them, and Dale hears about every one. Houses and stores don't break, but hitting one hard leaves a hole in the wall, a long talk with your supervisor and twenty minutes off your day. The crews put everything back overnight. Clock out at the Delivery Center to get paid and add the day to your career.

On foot. Park and press X (OUT on a phone) to step out and walk anywhere with W A S D, Shift to hurry. Walk up to a door with its package in your hands and you deliver it; F takes you back to the truck. The clock keeps running while you stroll.

Off the clock. Pick it on the title screen: no route, no radio, nobody keeping score, flames down the sides of the truck. Things still break. Get in people's way and they lean on the horn. Take the sidewalk and people scatter; the ones on their phones, the ones with earbuds in and the old folks don't always make it. Nobody gets hurt in Cedar Bend, but they get up hollering, and so does everybody who saw it, until you're far enough down the road. Every so often, once you have been driving a while, you can call one of them out (G), and now and then a driver pulls up and calls you out: G accepts, J declines (they will let you hear about it). In the street, pace on the count, and turn on the word (Space). Aim with the mouse (drag on a phone), click to fire, R or right-click to cock, Shift to steady your breath, A/D to sidestep. Turn early and the town remembers.

Past the edge of town. Hollow Rd keeps going north: past a few farms, under the Heights through the tunnel, and out into Hollow Valley. The map switches to the valley once you are up there. There are three places up there most people never find. Nothing at the road says where the tracks to them start.

Paused

End the shift now? Anything still on the truck counts as missed.

End of day

PACKAGE
CAR

Cedar Bend has a village under a ridge of firs and view houses, a strip of shops and warehouses, a freight line, and a long stretch of farms, forest and lake roads out past Tabor Butte, all in 3D and full of neighbors going about their day. Every morning the car leaves the center with a fresh, random load of about a hundred and forty stops. Drive the route, set the brake, find the piece, walk it to the door. Mind the dogs, humor the locals, keep the customers happy, and answer Dale on the radio.
